overview: Diarrhoeal disease is the third leading cause of death in children under 5 years old, responsible for killing around 443,832 children every year. Diarrhoea can last several days and can leave the body without the water and salts that are necessary for survival. It is usually a symptom of an infection in the intestinal tract, which can be caused by a variety of bacterial, viral and parasitic organisms.
symptoms: Passage of 3 or more loose or liquid stools per day
Unable to drink or drink poorly
Skin pinch goes back very slowly
diagnosis: Clinical evaluation of stool frequency and consistency
Laboratory tests to identify bacterial, viral and parasitic pathogens
treatment: Rehydration with oral rehydration salts (ORS) solution
transmission: Person-to-person contact due to poor hygiene
Unsafe domestic water storage and handling
Food prepared or stored in unhygienic conditions
prevention: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months of life
Health education about how infections spread
risk_factors: Lack of access to improved drinking-water and sanitation
key_facts: There are nearly 1.7 billion cases of childhood diarrhoeal disease every year
Diarrhoea is a leading cause of malnutrition in children under 5 years old
